mike: Heads-up — bringing up lyra-40k-int3 on staging. Hit reproducible kv-index drift after ~30.7k tokens when priming with a rhythm of short header / long doc / short header. suspect rotary-phase aliasing + quant packing.

mike: minimal repro (staging):
```
# run harness minimal
python -m tests.kvcache_repro --model lyra-40k-int3 --quant int3 --prefill tests/data/rhythm_short_long.txt --max-tokens 31000 --kv-inspect --kv-dump 6:6 --kv-shard 4
```

tara: did you try preserve-order? async prefetch merge has caused similar "slot shuffle" before.

mike: not yet. float32 run is clean, so it's quant+rotary related. model cfg: rotary_base=10000.0, pos_scale=1.011, rotary_exponent_clip=1e-7, rotary_interp=linear. kv args default tiled: --kv-tile 256 --kv-stride 32.

june: paste the tiny kv dump around the divergence please (5 lines).

mike: trimmed kv dump around idx~30720:
```
idx 30718 slot 1023 key=0x7b2a fp=0xc81a29
idx 30719 slot 1024 key=0x7b2b fp=0xc81a2a
idx 30720 slot 1025 key=0x7b2c fp=0xc81a2b -> AFTER_PREFILL fp=0xc81a2c
idx 30721 slot 1026 key=0x7b2d fp=0xc81a2d
```

rotary-bot: Canary deploy started: lyra-40k-int3 int3 -> staging (canary-id: c-20260912-5). Logs: /var/log/onboard/lyra/c-5.log :gear:

tara: if the fp increments by 1 consistently, check two things: 1) tiled-mapper slot aliasing when kv stride > 1, 2) atomic-insert ordering in async prefetcher. Also run with `--kv-atomic-insert true` to force compare-and-swap insertion to detect races.

june: try dense mapping (`--kv-stride 1 --kv-tile 65536`) and `--preserve-order true`. if dense mapping stops the bump, it's mapping arithmetic. if preserve-order stops it, it's ordering/race.

mike: kicked off three variants: preserve-order, dense-mapping, atomic-insert. added a compact CSV dumper printing `idx,slot,key,fp_before,fp_after,nearby_tokens` per line to help diffs. ETA ~18m.

eli: also try `rotary_interp=nearest` and tiny pos_scale tweaks (1.0, 1.005). interpolation can amplify quantized phase noise at large exponents which looks like index drift but is actually phase aliasing leading to different key material.

june: good point. if nearest fixes it, we should add an eval comparing token-similarity on long prefills across interpolations and quant levels.

tara: if atomic-insert surfaces a CAS failure, log owner info and abort the run — we want a fast assert to catch slot races in CI. add `--kv-slot-sanity-check` to runs.

mike: re-ran with preserve-order=true and kv-stride=1. preserve-order removed the bump in that run; dense-mapping also removed it. atomic-insert run shows occasional CAS failures in prefetcher v2.

mike: short log from preserve-order run (clean):
```
idx 30720 fp_before=0xc81a2b fp_after=0xc81a2b (match)
gen: no mismatch up to max-tokens
```

mike: short log from atomic-insert run (CAS failures):
```
[2026-09-12T16:04:12Z] kv_prefetcher: CAS failure slot=1025 existing_key=0x7b2c new_key=0x7b2c_owner=thread-7
[2026-09-12T16:04:12Z] kv_prefetcher: merge_resolve: reordered insertion detected -> bump
```

eli: looks like an insertion-order race where quant packing changes memory alignments such that concurrent insertions sometimes reorder. preserve-order masks it by serializing prefill writes. dense mapping reduces slot sharing so it masks collisions.

june: next steps: 1) add `--kv-slot-sanity-check` to CI for long-prefill onboarding tests (fail-fast on slot collisions), 2) fix prefetcher CAS backoff to linearized insertion order, 3) add interpolation/quant sensitivity harness to our onboarding checklist.

tara: agree. also add a small unit test that repeatedly runs concurrent prefetch inserts with different packing alignments (int3/int4 variants) to trigger the race in CI.

mike: opening PR with a small prefetcher fix and kv-slot-sanity-check toggle. will attach reproducible minimal harness and CSV diffs to the PR. thanks all. :white_check_mark:
